title: Final Cut Pro MCP: How to Set It Up (2026 Guide)
summary: Final Cut Pro MCP is a community-built bridge that lets AI send commands to the video editor. Evaluate whether this third-party tool suits your workflow.
body_markdown:
## Final Cut Pro MCP requirements, costs and permissions


Before anything else, check the macOS version: the hard gate sits on Final Cut Pro, not on the MCP.


Three integrations each carry their own price, operating system floor and permissions, and the table shows what to confirm for each before you install anything, so if your system's OS version is below an integration's floor, that integration cannot be used.


Figures were checked on 2026-11-16.


Price Minimum macOS Hardware Licence Permissions Maker source


Final Cut Pro $299.99 one-time, 30-day trial 26.2 for version 12 8GB RAM, 6.5GB disk Proprietary Standard app; the controlling process needs your approval to drive it Apple's Final Cut Pro tech specs page


MCP client Depends on your plan Set by the client's own release Set by the client Set by the client Asks before each tool call, if configured The client's MCP documentation


Server project Free to download if open source Read the README Runs beside the editor Read the licence file Expect macOS Accessibility or Automation prompts The project's repository


### Apple: Final Cut Pro price, trial and macOS requirement


At $299.99 once, with a 30-day free trial through Apple Creator Studio, Final Cut Pro lets you test the whole bridge before paying, so you have 30 days to determine if a $300 investment is worthwhile. The catch is the operating system.


According to the release notes collected by[Larry Jordan, Appleosophy and FCP Cafe](https://github.com/CommandPost/FCPCafe/blob/main/docs/releasenotes.md) , Final Cut Pro 10.6 needs macOS 11.5, version 11 needs 14.6 and version 12 needs 26.2.


Each release raises the floor, so a Mac that runs version 11 may be unable to run version 12.


Check your macOS first, because an upgrade to run the editor can break other software. Then confirm the 8GB of RAM and 6.5GB of free disk, since insufficient space or RAM will block installation.


### The AI client: plans and versions that support MCP


Don't look to Final Cut Pro for MCP support; it is a property of the client. Some clients gate it by plan, and many only added it in a particular version.


Open the client's own MCP documentation and confirm that your plan and version can add a local server. A client that can't will fail silently, and you'll blame the server.


Check whether the client asks for approval before each tool call. For an editor with your project open, you want that on.


### The server: runtime, licence and maintenance activity


Read three things in the repository: the runtime it needs (Node, Python or something else), the licence file, and the date of the most recent change. A project untouched since Final Cut Pro 11 may not know about version 12.


Most of all, mind the permissions it asks for. Accessibility access lets one process control another app, so grant it only to a server whose code you have read.


### Where to find candidate servers


Search GitHub for "final cut pro mcp" and sort the results by recently updated. Then check the public MCP registries, which list community servers by name. A registry listing is a pointer, not an endorsement, so the repository is still what you vet.


I could not verify any specific community server for this guide, meaning one whose route, runtime and last-commit date I could confirm on 16 November 2026. I name none rather than guess.


For each candidate you find, write down its route (FCPXML or UI automation), its runtime and the date of its last commit before you install.


### Final Cut Pro MCP server vetting checklist


A candidate should pass every item before you start Stage 1.


1. Its tool list names the actions you need, and nothing you don't.
2. It states its route, FCPXML or UI automation.
3. It names a runtime you can install and check on your Mac.
4. It has a licence file that permits your use.
5. Its last commit is recent enough to cover your version of Final Cut Pro.
6. You have read the source, and the permissions it asks for match what it does.
